system.name: MoEvement
system.one_liner: sparse checkpointing for fast and reliable Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) training

content.subject: how Upstream Logging shrinks pipeline-failure recomputation from a full cluster-wide rollback to just the failed worker

content.key_idea: By locally logging cross-stage activations and gradients, MoEvement lets only the failed pipeline worker replay and recover instead of rolling back the whole pipeline, cutting recovery time by 23%.
content.reading_order: left to right within each row: (a) compares the full three-stage rollback scope (dashed red box) against the narrowed single-stage (W1) scope; (b) below repeats the comparison as 1F1B Gantt schedules, ending in the 23% callout on the right

summary: This two-part figure contrasts MoEvement's Upstream Logging against dense checkpointing's cluster-wide rollback. In (a), a three-stage pipeline (W0/W1/W2, each running a Layer with a gating module G routing to experts E1-E4) is shown with a dashed red box marking the recomputation scope: without Upstream Logging it spans all three stages, but with it, only the failed stage W1 is rolled back, replaying from the Activation Log kept by upstream W0 and the Gradient Log kept by downstream W2. In (b), paired 1F1B Gantt schedules make the same contrast concrete over time: without Upstream Logging, all three workers replay many forward (blue) and backward (green) passes with long bubbles before the optimizer step; with it, only W1's row is active, shrinking the recovery window and yielding the 23% faster recovery called out on the right.
summary_zh: 该图对比MoEvement的Upstream Logging与稠密检查点：(a)故障恢复范围从全部三阶段缩小到仅失败的W1，靠上下游的激活/梯度日志重放；(b)配对1F1B甘特图显示W1恢复窗口大幅缩短，实现23%更快恢复。
notes: content.groups kept as the prior label's ['evolution'] (before/after variant): the 'without/with Upstream Logging' framing is read as a before-after state change of the same recovery procedure rather than a design-space comparison. layout.panel_count is set to 4 (2 views x 2 states) even though the index's coarse panel count is 2, because the figure visibly nests a without/with split inside each of the two labelled sub-figures (a) and (b).
